clinical_category: Severe eosinophilic asthma biologic therapy - mepolizumab mechanism
blueprint_topic: Targeted biologic pharmacology and maintenance treatment of severe eosinophilic asthma
stem: A client with severe eosinophilic asthma receives mepolizumab (NUCALA) as add-on maintenance therapy. Which mechanism best describes this medication?

options.A: It binds interleukin-5 and inhibits IL-5 signaling, reducing eosinophil production and survival
options.B: It stimulates beta2-adrenergic receptors to provide rapid bronchodilation during an acute attack
options.C: It antagonizes muscarinic receptors on bronchial smooth muscle
options.D: It blocks cysteinyl leukotriene type-1 receptors to inhibit LTD4 signaling

rationale: A is correct. The current NUCALA prescribing information identifies mepolizumab as an IL-5 antagonist. Section 12.1 states that it binds IL-5, blocks IL-5 binding to the alpha chain of the IL-5 receptor complex, inhibits IL-5 signaling, and reduces eosinophil production and survival. Section 1.1 specifies add-on maintenance treatment for severe asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype and states that NUCALA is not indicated for relief of acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus. B, C, and D describe other respiratory drug mechanisms and do not apply to mepolizumab.
educational_objective: Recognize mepolizumab as an IL-5 antagonist biologic used as add-on maintenance therapy for severe eosinophilic asthma, not as an acute bronchodilator.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine (DailyMed; FDA-approved biologic prescribing information)
source_document_title: NUCALA (mepolizumab) for injection/injection, for subcutaneous use
source_version_date: DailyMed page updated 2025-08-06; prescribing information revised 2025-08; current label accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: DailyMed Set ID fefb887c-e4ac-431e-8893-e9d1a5a63fea. Section 1.1 'Maintenance Treatment of Severe Asthma': add-on maintenance treatment for severe asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype; not for relief of acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus. source_claim_supported: The current official NUCALA label directly supports IL-5 antagonism, eosinophil reduction, the severe eosinophilic-asthma maintenance indication, and exclusion of acute rescue use.

correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The secondary PMC source was replaced by the current official NUCALA label. The item was narrowed from a biologic class generalization to mepolizumab specifically, and distractors were rebuilt as real competing respiratory-drug mechanisms.
audit_findings: The source used a secondary review despite an adequate current primary prescribing-information source.
Current NUCALA labeling directly verifies both the IL-5 mechanism and the severe eosinophilic-asthma add-on maintenance indication.
The final item avoids generalizing the mechanism across all asthma biologics and tests mepolizumab specifically.
All distractors represent distinct real respiratory pharmacologic mechanisms and none is defensible for mepolizumab.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no acute-rescue ambiguity, no cueing, no unsupported precision, and no unresolved source conflict.
